posts.name: Akankshya Sinha
posts.cooked:
You have a large log file, server.log , and you want the total count of the number of occurrences of the words “ERROR” and “WARNING” in the file. Which of the following command sequences will accomplish this?

For command grep
-c, --count
Suppress normal output; instead print a count of matching lines for each input file. With the
-v, --invert-match option (see
below), count non-matching lines.
In command wc
-l, --lines
print the newline counts

1

grep -E "ERROR|WARNING" server.log | wc -l

1

cat server.log | grep "ERROR" | grep "WARNING" | wc -l

1

grep -c "ERROR" server.log && grep -c "WARNING" server.log

1

grep -E "ERROR|WARNING" server.log | wc -w

correct ans- option 1 and 4

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked: What was our question here? Can you please elaborate.

posts.name: Akankshya Sinha
posts.cooked: Sir, i wanted to know how the answer is option 1 and 4, if we are counting the no. of occurences. It should only be option 4 since we are counting the no. of times the word ERROR/WARNING occurs. Option 1 counts the no. of lines containg word ERROR/WARNING, so we might miss to count those words occuring more than once in a line.

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked: In option 1 we are filtering the lines which have the word ERROR or WARNING with grep. And then after that we count the total number of lines, which will give us the count of how many times these words have been used.

posts.name: Akankshya Sinha
posts.cooked: Yes sir, the total number of lines will be counted. But if any of those lines contains ERROR/WARNING more than once, will those occurences be counted?

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked:
No those will not be counted. The correct answer to this question actually depends on the format of the log file.

  • Option 1 is only correct if we assume that the words are not repeated. Which is anyways not repeated in log files generally.
  • Option 4 is only correct, if we assume each line contains only one word. If the lines have more than one word then option 4 is also wrong.

posts.name: Akankshya Sinha
posts.cooked: Ok sir. Got it. Thank You
